The following conditions must be met:

Inclusion criteria:

  * Primary clinical cases of large B-cell lymphoma
  * Dogs weighing at least 10 kg and no more than 50 kg and > 12 months of age
  * Dogs must be naïve to treatment
  * Written consent for entry to the trial from each dog’s owner/designee

Not eligible:

  * Dogs with medical illness other than large B-cell lymphoma that, in the opinion of the investigator, could compromise evaluation of study endpoints
  * Dogs having received previous chemotherapy, radiation therapy, immunotherapy, and/or other treatments for lymphoma, including prednisone administration for > 14 days.
  * Dogs in the care of owners/designee living at a distance from the treatment center that will interfere with compliance with the treatment and follow-up schedule.

Dogs will undergo preliminary staging tests including initial consultation, physical examination, lab work, chest x-rays and abdominal ultrasound to determine trial eligibility. The IVP will be administered by mouth at home on a daily basis. Dogs will be required to return to UGA for recheck once weekly for 4 weeks, then every 2 weeks through the end of the study. The entire study period is 84 days. All rechecks and treatments must be performed at the University of Georgia Veterinary Teaching Hospital. Thereafter, dogs will exit the study. The costs of initial screening, follow-up visits, and IVP will be provided as part of the study.

Duration of study:

The study is currently OPEN.

Potential benefits to veterinary medicine:

Lymphoma is one of the most commonly diagnosed cancers in dogs. While conventional chemotherapy induces remission in the majority of dogs with multicentric lymphoma, relapses are common. Successful demonstration of efficacy and safety of this novel treatment will provide an important drug in the veterinarian’s armamentarium and a valuable option for pet owners seeking cancer treatment for their pets.

# Clinical Study for Cats with Mammary Cancer - Information for referring veterinarians

## Why refer your patients?

  * The therapy (GCN2-IN-6) has been carefully tested in preclinical studies and is well-tolerated.
  * Your referred patients will receive standard surgical care plus the investigational therapy.
  * Participation contributes valuable data for advancing cancer treatments in both cats and humans.

## Study design highlights

  * Neo-adjuvant and adjuvant therapy administered around the time of mastectomy.

  * Safety and efficacy are continuously monitored.

  * Feline mammary adenocarcinoma is a validated model for TNBC research.

## Referral process

  * Eligible cats: cats diagnosed with mammary tumors, eligible for surgery.

  * As referring veterinarians, you can retain primary responsibility for routine care; the study team coordinates treatment administration and follow-up.

  * Participation is voluntary, and owners can withdraw at any time.

## Impact:

By referring cats to this study, you are helping advance cutting-edge cancer research, improve therapeutic options, and potentially enhance outcomes for both feline and human patients.

## Contact

Further information can be obtained by mailing Ada Krupa (adriana.krupa@ugent.be) or Hilde de Rooster (hilde.derooster@ugent.be) or by phone (+32 9 264 77 00).

L’unité de formation doctorale Science et Médecine Vétérinaires (SMV) relève de l’école doctorale Sciences de la Vie et de la Santé. Elle a été constituée par la décision n° 2023/932 du 6 décembre 2023 portant restructuration des UFD.

Établissements co-accrédités selon l’appel à candidatures du 16 septembre 2025 : FS, ENSAI, ESMV, IUT, EGEM, EGCIM.

L’UFD comprend un coordonnateur, un Comité d’orientation, des responsables pédagogiques de masters recherche et des responsables pédagogiques de doctorats (décision n° 036-2025, art. 12).

## Missions

Selon l’article 11 de la décision n° 036-2025 du 2 décembre 2025, l’UFD a pour missions :

  * de proposer, au sein de son école doctorale, des offres de formation en Master et en Doctorat organisées selon le système LMD, par domaine, mention, parcours et spécialités ou options ;
  * de participer aux activités de formation et d’encadrement par la recherche ;
  * d’organiser les échanges scientifiques entre les doctorants et la communauté scientifique ;
  * de favoriser l’animation pédagogique et la gestion des programmes de formation ;
  * de favoriser le suivi et l’amélioration des conditions de travail et d’encadrement des étudiants de Master et des doctorants ;
  * d’assurer une démarche qualité de la formation ;
  * d’organiser des stages, des séminaires, des ateliers ou des journées scientifiques.
